streams.title: Microsoft Graph: Switch to App-Only Permissions for Secure Apps
streams.description:
Are you tired of your Microsoft 365 automations breaking every time a user changes their password or logs out? Many IT pros fall into the trap of using delegated permissions for background tasks, leading to constant support tickets and failed workflows. In this video, we dive deep into why app-only permissions are the secret to building secure, reliable, and set-it-and-forget-it integrations with Microsoft Graph.

We start by breaking down the hidden security traps of delegated permissions. While they might seem like the easiest way to get a flow or bot running, they tie your critical business processes to individual human accounts. When those users leave the company, change roles, or rotate their credentials, your automation grinds to a halt. We discuss how a massive percentage of custom app support tickets boil down to these authentication hurdles rather than the actual app logic.

Next, we explore the smarter path: app-only permissions. By treating your application as its own identity within Azure AD, you can ensure your SharePoint syncs, Teams notifications, and background jobs run 24/7 without needing a user to be logged in. You will learn how to apply the principle of least privilege to keep your environment secure while avoiding the temptation to grant global admin rights just to make things work.

The video also provides a walkthrough of the setup process, from registering your app in the Azure portal to handling the crucial admin consent step. We cover the common gotchas that lead to cryptic error messages and show you how to properly secure your client secrets using tools like Azure Key Vault. Finally, we look at real-world scenarios involving webhooks and the Microsoft Graph toolkit to help you scale your automation landscape.
